subject: Proposal: async fulfillment + usage visibility for Biolabs AWS Marketplace listing
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara@amazon.com>, Biolabs Procurement <procurement@biolabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Sep 2026 08:13:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: async fulfillment + usage visibility for Biolabs AWS Marketplace listing

Hi Lara, hi Biolabs team —

Thanks for the quick sync last week. Per our call, attached is a concise proposal for how Redwood and Biolabs can implement marketplace metering + async fulfillment while preserving invoice-level visibility for Biolabs' finance team. High level:

- Goal: Offer Biolabs as a SaaS listing on AWS Marketplace with per-tenant metering events routed to AWS and mirrored to Biolabs for downstream billing reconciliation.
- Fulfillment approach: Marketplace metering events (usage records) will be emitted from Biolabs' service, routed to Redwood for enrichment (SKU mapping + tenant metadata), and posted to AWS Usage API. For customers who want a pass-through invoice from Biolabs/Redwood (vs AWS consolidated billing), we propose a reconciliation export delivered daily to Biolabs' SFTP endpoint.
- Edge cases we call out: delayed usage events (replay window), orphaned tenant IDs (mapping failures), and multi-SKU sessions that require split-metering. Proposed mitigations are in the attached CSV.

Questions / asks for AWS:
- Does the Marketplace acceptance process allow the daily reconciliation artifact approach (Biolabs receives detailed usage CSV, AWS still receives metering events)? Any objections from fulfillment?
- For entitlements: can AWS propagate the marketplace entitlement token to the SaaS fulfillment callback, or should we expect to exchange an entitlement ID through the entitlement service?
- Any specific expectations for the usage record schema (tenant identifier length, timestamp timezones)?

Biolabs — please confirm your preferred billing contact and whether you can accept SFTP deliveries of the reconciliation files (or if a secure API is preferred).

Attachments: sku_mapping_proposal.csv, timelines_and_dependencies.pdf

Proposed timeline (tentative): 2 weeks for schema alignment + test metering, 1 week for contract amendment, 1 week for acceptance testing.

Next step: Lara — would you and aws-marketplace-support flag any immediate blockers? If not, we'd like to open a formal fulfillment ticket and circulate a short contract amendment for Biolabs' procurement.

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Marketplace Integrations
Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

From: Lara Chen <lara@amazon.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Biolabs Procurement <procurement@biolabs.com>
Cc: aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: async fulfillment + usage visibility for Biolabs AWS Marketplace listing

Jonas — thanks for the detailed proposal and attachments. High-level this approach can work, but a few clarifications before I move it into the internal fulfillment queue: 

1) Entitlement propagation: AWS Marketplace SaaS integrations usually surface an entitlement token in the SaaS fulfillment callback (Marketplace SaaS system). However, we recommend having a tenant-mapping layer on your side — the token is opaque and sometimes differs across renewals. Please confirm how Redwood plans to store and rotate the mapping.

2) Usage schema: AWS requires usage records to contain a unique usageDimension and a usageQuantity (decimal allowed). Tenant identifiers are customer-provided; we typically cap the ID length to 128 chars. If you plan to include timezone info, use ISO 8601 UTC timestamps.

3) Reconciliation artifact: AWS doesn't prevent partners from exchanging reconciliation files with sellers. That said, the acceptance team will want to see that reconciliation is reproducible and that the reconciliation keys map back to usage records sent to AWS. Include a sample 7-day export during onboarding.

4) Contract/Procurement: For sellers that invoice customers directly, we ask for an amendment that documents the fulfillment flow & invoicing model. We don't require DocuSign specifics but often see sellers attach an AWS Marketplace Evidence spreadsheet.

I'll open a fulfillment intake ticket after you provide: (a) a sample 7-day reconciliation CSV, (b) confirmation of tenant-id length and storage policy, and (c) the draft amendment language (PDF or DOCX). Once I have those, I'll route to the acceptance team and loop in the Marketplace Support channel for any policy exceptions.

Lara
Senior Partner Manager, AWS Marketplace
lara@amazon.com
